title: Team Themis: The Surveillance Contractor Cartel That Pitched Spy Craft on American Critics

extractionLoop.stage1_upfrontSkim: Contractors stood to bill corporate clients — the Chamber of Commerce and Bank of America — for bespoke counter-intelligence campaigns, converting legal retainers paid to Hunton & Williams into surveillance-services revenue.
extractionLoop.stage2_structuralCompromise: The law firm of a sitting corporate counsel assembled a three-firm consortium to weaponize the same integration tradecraft sold to the security state, proposing infiltration and disinformation against domestic political opponents — a structural fusion of corporate legal privilege and intelligence contracting.
extractionLoop.stage3_informationFog: The proposals circulated privately among contractors and counsel until Anonymous breached HBGary Federal in February 2011 and published the internal documents; the consortium's bidding had been invisible to its targets and to regulators.
extractionLoop.stage4_monopolyWindfall: The consortium's pitch sought a standing surveillance franchise over the Chamber's and the bank's perceived opponents — a private-market extension of the national-security data monopoly that Palantir and its peers had built on public contracts.
extractionLoop.stage5_merseyWhitewash: The affair closed without contract, prosecution, or inquiry outcome: Palantir severed ties with HBGary, suspended the employee involved, and its CEO apologized publicly; the proposal was framed as a bid that never matured rather than a structural exhibit of intent.

closedLoopRatchet.inheritedFramework: Team Themis inherited the post-9/11 security-state contracting economy and its tradecraft — the fusion centers, the intelligence-community integration platforms, and the revolving door that staffed both — and aimed it at domestic corporate opponents.
closedLoopRatchet.newFrameworkCreated: The episode exposed, without creating, a market for domestic counter-surveillance services; the lasting framework was the demonstrated continuity between state surveillance platforms and their corporate deployment.
closedLoopRatchet.closedLoopRecirculation: The exposure cost the contractors little: Palantir's federal business grew thereafter, the same platforms rolled onward, and the corporate clients suffered reputational damage only through the leak they had commissioned the work to avoid.
closedLoopRatchet.enablesNextDossier: The proposal — written, priced, and pitched — stands as the documented bridge between the national-security data state and its domestic enforcement deployment, which later dossiers track through ICE and immigration data contracts.

decoyVsLedger.viralDecoy: The Anonymous-versus-HBGary internet drama — a story of hacker mischief, one executive's hubris, and embarrassed Twitter accounts.
decoyVsLedger.whyDecoyFails: The hacker-versus-hubris frame erases the document itself: a priced proposal from three intelligence-contracting firms, coordinated by corporate counsel, to surveil, infiltrate, and discredit named journalists, a union, and a nonprofit's supporters on behalf of two of America's largest institutions.
decoyVsLedger.documentedLedger: The documented ledger: the Team Themis proposals of late 2010 (Palantir, Berico, HBGary Federal), assembled by Hunton & Williams for the U.S. Chamber of Commerce and Bank of America, exposed February 2011 via the HBGary Federal breach, naming targets for infiltration, surveillance, and disinformation — with Palantir's severance of ties, employee suspension, and public apology as the corporate aftermath.
